newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan businessmen prepare to visit Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan businessmen prepare to visit Iraq.

text.p: Moroccan businessmen are preparing to travel to Iraq to try to sell their goods to Baghdad under a food-for-oil deal with the United Nations, official sources said on Monday.
Plans for the sales team were discussed at a recent meeting of professional associations and firms dealing with food and farm products, medicines and oil, a trade ministry statement said.

Iraq has released a list of products it seeks, some of which could not be met by Morocco and some such as pharmaceuticals for which Moroccan firms were not registered. "(But) some products such as milk and vegetables have already been the subject of sales contracts which are in the course of being realised," the ministry said.

The oil-for-food deal became effective on December 10. It enables Iraq to sell $2 billion of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian supplies to help offset the effects of sanctions imposed on Iraq since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Moroccan imports from Iraq reached 3.2 billion dirhams ($354 million), mainly oil, in 1989, before falling 50 percent in the last year, 1990, before the embargo.
Morocco's exports to Iraq were respectively worth 353 million dirhams in 1989 and 329 million the following year.
In 1991, King Hassan sent 1,300 troops to Saudi Arabia as part of the U.S.-allied forces against Bagdad but allowed opposition mass demonstrations in Morocco in support of President Saddam Hussein.
